quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): third-quarter order intake totaled JPY 83.0 billion, including a large order of approximately JPY 5.0 billion related to quantum computing; excluding this order, order intake was largely in line with the second quarter, indicating that demand remained solid. No significant changes observed in recent months; industrial orders continue to be strong while medical and life science demand has been generally flat over the past year. Executive Officer Ogasawara (presentation): the company believes the solid order environment continues, particularly for its AI data center-related businesses.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 order intake JPY 83.0 billion, incl. ~JPY 5.0 billion quantum computing order

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Building No. 5 of the opto-semiconductor factory began operations in June, resulting in approximately JPY 0.5 billion of depreciation expenses in the third quarter plus start-up and operating costs; fourth-quarter depreciation is expected to total approximately JPY 1.5 billion; the commencement of operations has proceeded according to plan. For next fiscal year the company continues to expect a depreciation increase close to the previously indicated approximately JPY 5.0 billion, although the final amount may be somewhat lower. Q3 operating profit decreased versus Q2 due to factors including this depreciation.
quarterly_data.figure: New Building No. 5 operating since June; Q3 depreciation ~JPY 0.5 billion, Q4 ~JPY 1.5 billion; next FY increase ~JPY 5.0 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): annual sales related to optical communications are approximately JPY 2.0 billion, currently a relatively small portion of total sales. The company supplies high-speed photodiodes to optical transceiver manufacturers; as AI data center investments expand the optical communications market is growing, and it is developing products for next-generation, higher-speed communication systems. Management recognizes the strong growth potential of optical communications and aims to strengthen its presence there by leveraging its photodetection technologies.

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Officer Ogasawara (presentation): FY2026 Q3 YTD sales by application vs a year earlier - industrial +JPY11 billion (+20.6%), medical-bio +JPY3.7 billion (+8.5%), analytical +JPY1.6 billion (+8.4%), measuring +JPY1.8 billion (+25.2%); academic research -JPY1.7 billion (-11.2%) on completion of a large-scale project; transport sales down 5.4% on demand fluctuations from certain customers. Industrial accounted for 60% of the JPY17.5 billion sales increase. Within industrial, factory automation sales rose JPY1.8 billion on servo motor encoder and servo amplifier control equipment demand supported by AI-related semiconductor investment; in medical-bio, radiographic testing rose JPY2.4 billion as customer inventory adjustments for X-ray CT equipment ran their course, and laboratory testing rose JPY1.3 billion on new NanoZoomer virtual slide scanners. Foreign exchange had a positive impact of JPY3 billion on operating profit.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial +20.6%, medical-bio +8.5%, analytical +8.4%, measuring +25.2%, academic -11.2%; FX +JPY3 billion to operating profit

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Officer Ogasawara (presentation): revised FY2026 sales forecasts by application - semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment JPY45.9 billion (light sources and sensors expected to remain strong on AI semiconductor demand); semiconductor failure analysis systems JPY12.6 billion (no significant change in demand, but delays in the timing of some shipments and customer acceptances factored in); non-destructive testing JPY20.6 billion (X-ray sources for electronic component and battery inspection, supported by AI data center demand); factory automation JPY9.4 billion; medical-bio JPY65.4 billion, analytical JPY27.8 billion, measuring JPY13.1 billion. Over the past two years semiconductor manufacturing and inspection sales grew at an annual rate of 18.5% and non-destructive testing sales at 12.6%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 forecast: semiconductor manufacturing and testing JPY45.9 billion; failure analysis JPY12.6 billion; NDT JPY20.6 billion; FA JPY9.4 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): no significant change in the components supplied for wafer inspection, but as advanced semiconductor processes become more complex the number of inspection steps keeps rising, driving demand for customers' inspection equipment. In failure analysis systems large-scale deployment in mass production remains at an early stage, with current demand mainly for analysis of leading-edge devices such as HBM. X-ray non-destructive inspection orders keep increasing on demand for more detailed inspection of circuit boards, particularly for AI servers; as a component supplier the company lacks full visibility of end use but believes AI data center investment has been a major driver over the past two years. Demand for EV battery inspection systems is increasing but has not returned to peak levels (still a recovery phase). Based on customer discussions it has not observed COVID-era style inventory-driven advance purchasing in semiconductor markets; demand is primarily supported by underlying end-market demand.

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): gross profit margin improved from 47.8% in the previous fiscal year to above 50% in the second quarter; since the third quarter, depreciation from newly commissioned facilities weighs on margins while higher volumes improve utilization. The full-year gross margin forecast was revised from 48.1% to 47.9%, mainly reflecting inventory disposal costs and more conservative expense assumptions; the forecast includes approximately JPY 1.0 billion in inventory disposal costs, so fourth-quarter profit growth is expected to be more modest than sales growth. Price revisions have developed as planned, with shipments from April onward contributing positively. Imaging and Measurement Instruments profitability fell short of the May forecast because shipments of high-margin failure analysis systems were delayed, plus higher material costs and mix. CCC was 264 days, 26 days better than 290 days at end-FY2025, against a 240-day target.
quarterly_data.figure: Gross margin forecast 47.9% (previous 48.1%); ~JPY 1.0 billion inventory disposal costs; CCC 264 days (target 240 days)

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): at Hamamatsu Photonics A/S (formerly NKT Photonics A/S) the plan to bring operating profit before goodwill amortization to break-even within three years remains on track, with a target of improving profitability by approximately JPY 1.0 billion annually; this fiscal year the improvement is reduced somewhat by higher quantum computing-related R&D, and the company aims for an operating profit improvement of more than JPY 1.0 billion next fiscal year. The Laser segment loss reflects quantum-technology R&D and foreign exchange effects; the business includes many project-based orders, so quarterly results fluctuate. The renaming is meant to reinforce group unity, integrate sales through Hamamatsu's global network, and combine the former NKT Photonics' light-generation expertise with Hamamatsu's photodetection strengths.
quarterly_data.figure: Profitability improvement target ~JPY 1.0 billion annually; more than JPY 1.0 billion next fiscal year

quarterly_data.quarter: Hamamatsu Photonics results briefing Q&A: Q3 FY2026 Results Briefing Script (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Officer Ogasawara (presentation) and management Q&A: the company supplies laser light sources, modulators and detectors for three of the four quantum computer approaches - neutral-atom, ion-trap and photonic - and positions quantum computing as a medium- to long-term growth area. In June 2026 it signed a memorandum of understanding with Yaqumo regarding advanced optical systems for quantum computing and is considering expanding from component supply into the systems field in the future. Management: interest in neutral-atom quantum computing is increasing, but it remains unclear which platform will dominate, so the company supports multiple architectures; its laser products are also widely used in ion-trap systems.
